source_scope.statement: For a topological space X, a sheaf O of unital possibly noncommutative rings, and left O-modules A and B, define the global morphism group Hom_O(A,B) and, for every arbitrary subspace U of X, Hom_O(U;A,B)=Hom_{O|U}(A|U,B|U).
source_scope.excluded_following_unit: The sheaf property on open subsets, equations (4.1.1)--(4.1.2), and the internal-Hom center-sheaf action begin at the next LayerTarget and are not silently part of this source unit.
other_exclusions: No stalk comparison, finite-type or pseudo-coherent assertion is included.
No Ext, derived-functor, or exactness assertion is included.
The arbitrary subset in the restricted-Hom definition is not weakened to an open subset.

source_defect.printed_claim: Hom_O(A,B) is a module over Z(Gamma(X,O)).
source_defect.reason: A section central in O(X) need not restrict to a central section of O(V), because local sections on V need not extend globally; multiplication by its restriction can therefore fail to be O|V-linear.

counterexample.space: The Sierpinski space X={x,y} with nonempty proper open U={y}.
counterexample.ring_sheaf: O(X)=Q[t], O(U)=M_2(Q), with restriction t mapped to D=diag(1,0).
counterexample.central_global_section: t lies in Z(O(X)), while D is not central in O(U).
counterexample.modules_and_map: Take A=B=O as left regular sheaves and f=id.
counterexample.failed_linearity: For h_U(M)=DM, s=E_12 and m=I give h_U(sm)=D E_12=E_12 but s h_U(m)=E_12 D=0.

source_defect.correct_replacement: Replace Z(Gamma(X,O)) by Gamma(X,O^natural), where O^natural is the sheaf-theoretic center: its sections over W remain central after restriction to every open V contained in W.
source_defect.maximality: Gamma(X,O^natural) is the largest subring of O(X) whose pointwise left-multiplication formula acts on Hom_O(A,B) for every pair of left O-modules.
source_defect.valid_special_case: The printed claim is valid when restrictions preserve centers, in particular when O is commutative.
